In its present form, 四 has an enclosing 囗 shape around inner 儿-form strokes; this visible structure does not establish the ancient identities or roles of those parts. Its origin remains disputed. One interpretation reads four horizontal marks as counting rods representing four, while another describes 亖 as a direct numeral. A competing proposal treats 四 as a graph depicting breath, identified with 呬, and later reused to write “four” because the words may have sounded alike; the depicted referent’s original name is unknown. A separate proposal treats 四 as the original graph of 泗, depicting nasal discharge, and says it was later borrowed to write “four”; this account lacks textual attestation. Neither borrowing explanation is established.
